course.title: Frontend Web Development
course.tagline: Build fast, beautiful websites with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and ship a portfolio that proves it.

days.title: How the Web Works and Your First Page
days.goal: Explain how browsers, servers and HTML fit together and build a first HTML page.

video.title: Complete Web Designing & Front-End Development Course in 10 Hours | HTML, CSS & JavaScript

steps: Install VS Code and create a folder called my-first-site.
Create index.html and type the basic skeleton: doctype, html, head, body.
Add an h1 heading and a paragraph about yourself, then open the file in a browser.
Change the heading text and refresh to see the page update.
days.task: Publish a one-page 'About me' HTML page with a heading, two paragraphs and a list of three hobbies.
days.challenge: Write the whole page from memory without copying, then compare it with the video.

quiz.q: What does HTML stand for?
quiz.explain: HTML is HyperText Markup Language, the language that structures web pages.

quiz.q: Which tag holds the visible content of a page?
quiz.explain: Everything users see goes inside <body>; <head> holds metadata.

quiz.q: What file name do browsers load first in a folder?
quiz.explain: Web servers serve index.html by default when no file is named.

days.title: Text, Links and Images
days.goal: Use headings, paragraphs, links and images to structure a real page.

video.title: HTML Crash Course For Absolute Beginners

steps: Add h1 to h3 headings to your page to create a clear outline.
Turn a word in a paragraph into a link with an <a> tag pointing to a real website.
Add an image with an tag, a src and a descriptive alt attribute.
Create an unordered list of your skills and an ordered list of your goals.
days.task: Build a page with at least 3 heading levels, 2 links, 1 image with alt text and both kinds of list.
days.challenge: Make every link open in a new tab and add a caption under your image using a <figure> tag.

quiz.q: Which attribute sets the image file in an tag?
quiz.explain: src (source) tells the browser which image file to load.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of alt text?
options: It describes the image for screen readers and when it fails to load
quiz.explain: Alt text describes the image for accessibility and as a fallback.

quiz.q: Which tag creates a numbered list?
quiz.explain: <ol> is an ordered (numbered) list; <ul> is unordered (bulleted).

days.title: Lists, Tables and Page Structure
days.goal: Organise content with lists, tables and semantic section tags.

video.title: Create a Simple Website with HTML, CSS, JavaScript

steps: Add a table with a header row showing a weekly schedule or price list.
Wrap your page content in <header>, <main> and <footer> tags.
Split the main content into <section> blocks with their own headings.
Add a <nav> with links that jump to each section using id attributes.
days.task: Create a schedule page with a 3-column table, a nav menu and three sections.
days.challenge: Add a second table that uses colspan to merge two cells in one row.

quiz.q: Which tag defines a table header cell?
quiz.explain: <th> marks a header cell; <td> is a normal data cell.

quiz.q: What does the <nav> element represent?
quiz.explain: <nav> wraps the main navigation links of a page.

quiz.q: How do you link to a section with id 'contact' on the same page?
quiz.explain: A hash plus the id, like #contact, jumps to that element.

days.title: Forms: Inputs, Labels and Buttons
days.goal: Build a working form with labelled inputs, dropdowns and a submit button.

video.title: Full Stack Web Development for Beginners

steps: Create a <form> with text inputs for name and email.
Connect every input to a <label> using the for and id attributes.
Add a dropdown <select> for country and radio buttons for a preference.
Add a textarea for a message and a submit button.
days.task: Build a contact form with name, email, country dropdown, one radio group, a message box and a submit button.
days.challenge: Add required attributes and a placeholder to every text input, then test submitting with a field empty.

quiz.q: Why should inputs have a matching <label>?
options: It improves accessibility and lets users click the label to focus the input
It is required for the form to submit
quiz.explain: Labels help screen readers and make inputs easier to click and focus.

quiz.q: Which input type checks that a value looks like an email?
quiz.explain: type='email' triggers built-in email format validation.

quiz.q: Which attribute makes a field mandatory?
quiz.explain: The required attribute blocks submission until the field is filled.

days.title: CSS Basics: Selectors and Colours
days.goal: Style a page with CSS selectors, colours, fonts and spacing.

video.title: Learn Web Development with This Free 20-Hour Course

steps: Create a styles.css file and link it in your HTML head.
Set the body font, background colour and text colour.
Style all h1 headings one way and give one paragraph a class for a different style.
Use an id selector to style a single standout element.
days.task: Style your 'About me' page: a font stack, two colours, styled headings and one highlighted box.
days.challenge: Recreate the same look using only class selectors, no element or id selectors.

quiz.q: How do you link an external stylesheet?
quiz.explain: <link rel='stylesheet' href='...'> connects a CSS file.

quiz.q: Which selector targets class 'card'?
quiz.explain: A dot targets a class; a hash targets an id.

quiz.q: Which property changes text colour?
quiz.explain: The color property sets the colour of text.

days.title: The Box Model: Margin, Padding and Borders
days.goal: Control layout spacing with the CSS box model.

video.title: Learn HTML and CSS by Building an Order Summary Component

steps: Give a div a width, padding, border and margin and inspect it in DevTools.
Add box-sizing: border-box to all elements and notice how widths behave.
Build a card with an image, heading, text and button, with padding inside and margin outside.
Centre the card on the page using margin: 0 auto and a max-width.
days.task: Build three cards in a row using the box model, each with padding, a border and a button.
days.challenge: Make the cards equal height without setting a fixed height on them.

quiz.q: What does padding do?
options: Space inside the border, between content and border
quiz.explain: Padding is inner space between content and border; margin is outer space.

quiz.q: What does box-sizing: border-box change?
quiz.explain: With border-box, the width you set includes padding and border, which is easier to predict.

quiz.q: Which property centres a block element horizontally?
quiz.explain: margin: 0 auto centres a block with a set width.

days.title: Project 1: Personal Profile Page
days.goal: Combine HTML and CSS into a finished personal profile page.

video.title: CSS Flexbox and Grid Tutorial

steps: Plan the page on paper: header, about, skills, contact.
Write semantic HTML for all four sections.
Style it with your own colour scheme, fonts and spacing.
Check the page at a narrow window width and fix anything that overflows.
days.task: Ship a complete profile page with a photo, bio, skills list and contact form, all styled.
days.challenge: Ask a friend to open the page and find one thing that is hard to read, then fix it.

quiz.q: What makes HTML semantic?
options: Using tags that describe the meaning of content, like <header> and <article>
quiz.explain: Semantic tags describe meaning, which helps accessibility and search engines.

quiz.q: Why check a page at narrow widths?
options: Phones are the most common way people browse
It makes the page load faster
quiz.explain: Most visitors browse on phones, so a page must work at small widths.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to check when a style does not apply?
options: Whether the stylesheet is linked and the selector matches
quiz.explain: A missing link or a wrong selector is the most common cause.

project.title: Personal Profile Page
project.brief: Build a complete personal profile page with semantic HTML and CSS: header with your name and photo, an about section, a skills list and a contact form.
checks: Page uses header, main, section and footer tags
At least one image with descriptive alt text
Contact form has labelled inputs and a submit button
Custom colours and fonts applied through an external stylesheet
Page has no horizontal overflow at 360px wide
All text is readable with good contrast

days.title: Flexbox: Lining Things Up
days.goal: Lay out content in rows and columns with Flexbox.

video.title: Flexbox vs Grid | Which One Should You Use & Why?

steps: Make a container display: flex and put three boxes inside it.
Use justify-content to spread the boxes apart, then centre them.
Use align-items to line the boxes up vertically.
Make a navigation bar with a logo on the left and links on the right using flex.
days.task: Build a nav bar and a row of three feature boxes using Flexbox.
days.challenge: Build the same row so the boxes wrap onto a second line on narrow screens.

quiz.q: What does display: flex do to an element's children?
options: Lays them out along a main axis you control
quiz.explain: Flexbox arranges children along a row or column with alignment controls.

quiz.q: Which property distributes space along the main axis?
quiz.explain: justify-content controls spacing along the main axis.

quiz.q: What does flex-wrap: wrap allow?
options: Items to move onto a new line when they run out of room
quiz.explain: wrap lets flex items flow onto extra lines instead of overflowing.

days.title: CSS Grid: Two-Dimensional Layouts
days.goal: Build page layouts with CSS Grid rows and columns.

video.title: Learn CSS Flexbox & CSS Grid Building This Dashboard - html and css (CSS Full course 2026)

steps: Create a grid container with three equal columns using repeat(3, 1fr).
Place a header that spans all three columns.
Use grid-template-areas to name regions: header, sidebar, main, footer.
Add a gap between grid cells.
days.task: Build a blog layout with a full-width header, a sidebar and a main article area using Grid.
days.challenge: Rebuild the same layout with Flexbox and note which one felt easier for this job.

quiz.q: What does 1fr mean in a grid track?
options: One fraction of the free space
quiz.explain: fr units share out the free space proportionally.

quiz.q: Which is Grid best suited for?
options: Two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns
quiz.explain: Grid controls rows and columns together; Flexbox is best for one direction.

quiz.q: What does grid-template-areas do?
options: Lets you name layout regions and place items by name
quiz.explain: Named areas let you describe a layout in a readable map.

days.title: Responsive Design and Media Queries
days.goal: Make layouts adapt to phones, tablets and desktops.

video.title: Become a Fullstack Developer from Scratch

steps: Add the viewport meta tag to your page head.
Write a media query that stacks a three-column grid into one column under 700px.
Make images responsive with max-width: 100%.
Test your page by resizing the browser and with DevTools device mode.
days.task: Take your blog layout and make it fully usable on a 360px-wide phone screen.
days.challenge: Add a second breakpoint at 1024px that changes the layout for tablets.

quiz.q: What does the viewport meta tag do?
options: It tells mobile browsers to use the device width for layout
quiz.explain: Without it, phones render the desktop layout zoomed out.

quiz.q: In a media query, what does max-width: 700px mean?
options: Apply these styles when the screen is 700px or narrower
Apply styles only on screens wider than 700px
quiz.explain: max-width applies the rules at that width and below.

quiz.q: Why use max-width: 100% on images?
options: It stops images overflowing narrow containers
quiz.explain: Responsive images shrink to fit their container instead of overflowing.

days.title: Transitions, Animations and Hover States
days.goal: Add motion and feedback with CSS transitions and keyframe animations.

video.title: Complete Web Designing & Front-End Development Course in 10 Hours | HTML, CSS & JavaScript

steps: Add a hover effect to a button that changes colour over 0.3s with transition.
Make a card lift slightly on hover using transform: translateY.
Create a @keyframes fade-in animation and apply it to a page heading.
Add a loading spinner using a rotating border animation.
days.task: Add hover states to every link and button on your profile page, plus one entrance animation.
days.challenge: Make the animation respect users who prefer reduced motion with a media query.

quiz.q: What does transition do?
options: It animates a property change smoothly over time
It moves an element to another page
quiz.explain: transition smooths the change between two states of a property.

quiz.q: Which property moves an element without changing layout?
quiz.explain: transform moves the visual rendering without disturbing surrounding layout.

quiz.q: What defines the steps of a keyframe animation?
quiz.explain: @keyframes lists the styles at each point of the animation.

days.title: CSS Variables and Design Tokens
days.goal: Build a consistent design system with CSS custom properties.

video.title: Learn CSS Variables In 7 Minutes

steps: Define --primary, --background and --text variables on :root.
Replace hard-coded colours across your stylesheet with the variables.
Add a dark theme by redefining the variables under a .dark class.
Add a button that toggles the .dark class with one line of JavaScript.
days.task: Convert your profile page to use CSS variables and add a working light/dark toggle.
days.challenge: Create a second colour theme (for example green and gold) by changing only the variables.

quiz.q: Where are CSS variables usually defined?
options: On :root so every element can use them
quiz.explain: :root is the document root, so variables defined there are global.

quiz.q: How do you use a variable called --primary?
quiz.explain: var() reads the value of a custom property.

quiz.q: Why use variables for colours?
options: One change updates the whole site consistently
quiz.explain: Variables keep a design consistent and easy to change in one place.

days.title: Accessibility and Semantic HTML
days.goal: Make pages usable for everyone, including keyboard and screen-reader users.

video.title: Create a Simple Website with HTML, CSS, JavaScript

steps: Check that every image has meaningful alt text and every input has a label.
Make sure all interactive elements can be reached and used with the Tab key.
Add a visible focus style so keyboard users can see where they are.
Test your page with a screen reader or the browser's accessibility checker.
days.task: Audit your profile page and fix at least five accessibility issues.
days.challenge: Navigate your whole site using only the keyboard and fix anything you cannot reach.

quiz.q: What is alt text for?
options: Describing images to people who cannot see them
quiz.explain: Alt text is read by screen readers so blind users understand images.

quiz.q: Why does focus visibility matter?
options: Keyboard users need to see which element is active
quiz.explain: Without a visible focus indicator, keyboard users cannot tell where they are.

quiz.q: Which heading order is correct?
options: h1, then h2, then h3 in order
quiz.explain: Headings should follow a logical order so screen readers can outline the page.

days.title: Project 2: Responsive Landing Page
days.goal: Design and build a polished responsive landing page for a real product.

video.title: Full Stack Web Development for Beginners

steps: Pick a product or service and sketch the landing page sections on paper.
Build the hero section with a headline, supporting text and a call-to-action button.
Add a features section with three cards and a testimonial section.
Make the whole page responsive with Flexbox, Grid and one media query.
days.task: Ship a complete landing page with hero, features, testimonials and a footer, working on phone and desktop.
days.challenge: Get one person to read the page for 10 seconds and tell you what the product does; fix it if they cannot.

quiz.q: What is the job of a hero section?
options: To explain the offer and get the visitor to act in seconds
quiz.explain: The hero must communicate value fast and lead to one clear action.

quiz.q: What makes a good call-to-action button?
options: Clear wording, strong contrast and one obvious next step
quiz.explain: A CTA should be unmissable and say exactly what happens next.

quiz.q: When should you add a media query?
options: When the layout breaks or looks wrong at a certain width
quiz.explain: Breakpoints belong where the design actually breaks, not at fixed device sizes.

project.title: Responsive Landing Page
project.brief: Design and build a landing page for a real product or service, with a hero, features, testimonials and footer, fully responsive.
checks: Hero has a clear headline, supporting text and one call-to-action
Features section uses Flexbox or Grid with three cards
Page works on a 360px phone screen without overflow
At least one media query adapts the layout
Hover states exist on links and buttons
Testimonial section is present with at least two quotes

days.title: JavaScript Basics: Variables and Data
days.goal: Write your first JavaScript: variables, types and console output.

video.title: Learn Web Development with This Free 20-Hour Course

steps: Create a script.js file and link it at the end of your HTML body.
Declare variables with let and const and log them to the console.
Try the main types: string, number, boolean, array and object.
Use template literals to build a sentence from variables.
days.task: Write a script that stores your name, age and three skills, then logs a sentence about yourself.
days.challenge: Swap two variables' values without using a third variable.

quiz.q: What is the difference between let and const?
options: let can be reassigned, const cannot
quiz.explain: const bindings cannot be reassigned; let bindings can.

quiz.q: Which of these is a string?
quiz.explain: Quotes make it a string; without quotes 42 is a number.

quiz.q: What does console.log do?
options: Prints a value to the browser console for debugging
quiz.explain: console.log outputs values to the developer console.

days.title: Functions and Scope
days.goal: Organise code into reusable functions.

video.title: Learn HTML and CSS by Building an Order Summary Component

steps: Write a function greet(name) that returns a greeting string.
Write a function that takes a price and a discount and returns the final price.
Use default parameters so a function works when an argument is missing.
Call your functions from different places and log the results.
days.task: Write five small utility functions (greet, add, multiply, isEven, fullName) and test each in the console.
days.challenge: Rewrite one function as an arrow function and confirm it still works.

quiz.q: What does return do in a function?
options: Sends a value back to the caller
quiz.explain: return passes a value out of the function to whoever called it.

quiz.q: What is a parameter?
options: A value passed into a function
quiz.explain: Parameters are the named inputs a function accepts.

quiz.q: What is an arrow function?
quiz.explain: Arrow functions use the => syntax and are a compact way to write functions.

days.title: The DOM: Selecting and Changing Elements
days.goal: Read and change page content with JavaScript and the DOM.

video.title: CSS Flexbox and Grid Tutorial

steps: Select an element by id with document.getElementById.
Change its text with textContent and its style with .style.
Select several elements with querySelectorAll and loop over them.
Create a new list item with JavaScript and add it to a page.
days.task: Build a page where a button changes the heading text, background colour and an image when clicked.
days.challenge: Change every list item on a page to uppercase using one loop.

quiz.q: What does document.querySelector('.card') return?
options: The first element with class card
quiz.explain: querySelector returns the first match; querySelectorAll returns all matches.

quiz.q: Which property changes an element's text safely?
quiz.explain: textContent sets plain text without parsing HTML, which is safer.

quiz.q: What is the DOM?
options: The browser's live representation of the page as objects JavaScript can change
quiz.explain: The DOM is the tree of objects the browser builds from HTML.

days.title: Events: Making Pages Interactive
days.goal: Respond to clicks, typing and other user actions.

video.title: Flexbox vs Grid | Which One Should You Use & Why?

steps: Add a click listener to a button that shows an alert or updates text.
Listen for the input event on a text field and mirror what the user types.
Add a mouseover effect that highlights a card.
Prevent a form from reloading the page with preventDefault().
days.task: Build a live character counter: as the user types in a textarea, show how many characters remain out of 200.
days.challenge: Add a button that toggles a dark theme class on the body.

quiz.q: What does addEventListener do?
options: Runs code when a chosen event happens on an element
quiz.explain: It registers a function to run when an event like click or input fires.

quiz.q: What does event.preventDefault() do?
options: Stops the browser's default action, like submitting a form
quiz.explain: It cancels the default behaviour, for example a form reload.

quiz.q: Which event fires every time a user types in a field?
quiz.explain: The input event fires on every keystroke and paste.

days.title: Arrays, Objects and Loops
days.goal: Store and process collections of data with arrays and objects.

video.title: Learn CSS Flexbox & CSS Grid Building This Dashboard - html and css (CSS Full course 2026)

steps: Create an array of five products, each an object with name and price.
Use a for loop to log every product name.
Use .map() to build an array of just the prices.
Use .filter() to keep only products under a price you choose.
days.task: Render a product list on a page from an array of objects, with name and price for each.
days.challenge: Sort the products by price and re-render the list.

quiz.q: Which method creates a new array by transforming each item?
quiz.explain: map returns a new array with each item transformed by your function.

quiz.q: How do you access the price of object product?
quiz.explain: Dot notation reads a property: product.price.

quiz.q: What does .filter() return?
options: A new array with only the items that pass a test
quiz.explain: filter returns a new array containing only matching items.

days.title: Conditionals and Logic in Practice
days.goal: Use if/else and logical operators to make decisions in code.

video.title: Become a Fullstack Developer from Scratch

steps: Write a function that returns a grade letter from a score.
Use && and || to combine two conditions in one if statement.
Use a ternary operator for a short either-or value.
Handle an empty input by showing an error message instead of crashing.
days.task: Build a small discount checker: enter a price and a code, and show the correct final price or an error.
days.challenge: Add a third discount code with a different percentage.

quiz.q: What does === check?
options: Value and type, without converting types
quiz.explain: Strict equality checks both value and type; == converts types first.

quiz.q: When does an else block run?
options: When the if condition is false
quiz.explain: else runs only when its matching if condition is false.

quiz.q: What does && mean?
options: AND — both sides must be true
quiz.explain: && is logical AND; both sides must be true for the whole thing to be true.

days.title: Project 3: Interactive Quiz App
days.goal: Build a working quiz app with questions, scoring and feedback.

video.title: Complete Web Designing & Front-End Development Course in 10 Hours | HTML, CSS & JavaScript

steps: Store five quiz questions as an array of objects with options and a correct answer.
Render one question at a time with clickable answer buttons.
Track the score and show feedback after each answer.
Show a final results screen with the score and a restart button.
days.task: Ship a quiz app with at least 5 questions, live scoring and a results screen.
days.challenge: Add a 10-second timer per question that moves on automatically when time runs out.

quiz.q: Why store questions as data instead of hard-coding HTML?
options: The same rendering code can show any question, so adding questions is easy
quiz.explain: Data-driven rendering separates content from code and scales easily.

quiz.q: How do you track a quiz score in JavaScript?
options: In a variable that increases when an answer is correct
quiz.explain: A score variable is updated as the user answers.

quiz.q: What should happen after the last question?
options: Show the final score and a way to restart
quiz.explain: A results screen closes the loop and lets the user try again.

project.title: Interactive Quiz App
project.brief: Build a quiz app in JavaScript with at least five questions, live scoring, feedback after each answer and a results screen.
checks: Questions stored as data, not hard-coded HTML
One question shown at a time with clickable answers
Score updates live and is shown at the end
Feedback appears after each answer
A restart button starts a new round
App works without console errors

days.title: Fetch API and Working with JSON
days.goal: Load real data from an API and show it on a page.

video.title: Fetch API & Rendering Data with JavaScript

steps: Use fetch() to request data from a public JSON API.
Convert the response with .json() and log the result.
Handle errors with .catch() and show a friendly message.
Render the fetched items as cards on the page.
days.task: Build a page that fetches a list of posts or users from a public API and displays them as cards.
days.challenge: Add a search box that filters the fetched results as you type.

quiz.q: What does fetch() return?
options: A Promise that resolves to a response
quiz.explain: fetch returns a Promise; you await it and then parse the body.

quiz.q: What is JSON?
options: A text format for structured data
quiz.explain: JSON is a lightweight text format for sending structured data.

quiz.q: Why use .catch() with fetch?
options: To handle network failures and show a useful message
quiz.explain: Network requests can fail, so errors must be handled gracefully.

days.title: Saving Data with Local Storage
days.goal: Persist user data in the browser with localStorage.

video.title: Create a Simple Website with HTML, CSS, JavaScript

steps: Save a value with localStorage.setItem and read it back with getItem.
Store an object by converting it with JSON.stringify.
Load saved data when the page opens and restore the page state.
Add a button that clears the saved data.
days.task: Build a notes app that saves notes to localStorage and restores them after a refresh.
days.challenge: Add a delete button for each note that also updates storage.

quiz.q: What does localStorage do?
options: Stores key-value data in the browser that survives refreshes
quiz.explain: localStorage keeps data in the browser across sessions.

quiz.q: Why use JSON.stringify before saving an object?
quiz.explain: localStorage stores strings, so objects must be serialised first.

quiz.q: How do you remove one saved item?
quiz.explain: removeItem deletes one key; clear() wipes everything.

days.title: Form Validation with JavaScript
days.goal: Validate forms in JavaScript and show helpful error messages.

video.title: Full Stack Web Development for Beginners

steps: Listen for the form submit event and stop the default reload.
Check that the name is at least 2 characters and the email contains @.
Show a red error message under any invalid field.
Show a green success message when the form is valid.
days.task: Build a sign-up form with live validation for name, email and password strength.
days.challenge: Add a rule that the password must be at least 8 characters with a number.

quiz.q: Why validate on the client as well as the server?
options: Client validation gives instant feedback; server validation is the real security
It is faster to skip the server
quiz.explain: Client checks improve experience; server checks protect the data.

quiz.q: What is a good way to show an error?
options: Inline text next to the field, in a clear colour
quiz.explain: Inline messages tell the user exactly which field to fix.

quiz.q: When should validation run?
options: On submit and as the user types, for the best experience
quiz.explain: Live feedback plus a final submit check gives the best experience.

days.title: Deploying Your Site and Using Git
days.goal: Put your work online with Git and a free host.

video.title: Learn Web Development with This Free 20-Hour Course

steps: Initialise a Git repository in your project folder and make your first commit.
Create a free GitHub account and push your project to a repository.
Deploy the site with GitHub Pages or Netlify Drop.
Share the live link and test it on your phone.
days.task: Deploy your portfolio site live and push the code to GitHub.
days.challenge: Make a small change, commit it and redeploy to see the update go live.

quiz.q: What does git commit do?
options: Saves a snapshot of your changes in local history
quiz.explain: A commit records a snapshot you can return to later.

quiz.q: What is GitHub Pages?
options: Free hosting for static sites from a GitHub repository
quiz.explain: GitHub Pages serves a static site directly from your repo.

quiz.q: Why use version control?
options: It tracks changes and lets you undo mistakes safely
quiz.explain: Version control gives you a history and a safe way to roll back.

days.title: Performance, SEO and Best Practice
days.goal: Make sites fast, findable and well organised.

video.title: Learn HTML and CSS by Building an Order Summary Component

steps: Add a title tag and meta description to every page.
Compress your images and use the right format for each one.
Remove unused CSS and check your page load in DevTools.
Add semantic headings and alt text so search engines understand the page.
days.task: Audit your portfolio for speed and SEO and fix at least five issues.
days.challenge: Get a Lighthouse score in DevTools and improve it by 10 points.

quiz.q: What is a meta description?
options: A short summary of the page shown in search results
quiz.explain: The meta description is the snippet search engines may show under your link.

quiz.q: Why compress images?
options: Smaller files load faster, especially on slow connections
quiz.explain: Large images are the most common cause of slow pages.

quiz.q: What does Lighthouse measure?
options: Performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO
quiz.explain: Lighthouse audits a page across performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO.

days.title: Debugging Like a Developer
days.goal: Find and fix bugs systematically with DevTools.

video.title: CSS Flexbox and Grid Tutorial

steps: Open the console and read an error message to find the failing line.
Use console.log at key points to trace what your code is doing.
Set a breakpoint in the Sources panel and step through code.
Fix a bug by changing one thing at a time and re-testing.
days.task: Deliberately break a working page in three ways, then find and fix each bug using DevTools.
days.challenge: Explain each bug and its fix in one sentence each, as if teaching a friend.

quiz.q: What is a breakpoint?
options: A point where code pauses so you can inspect values
quiz.explain: Breakpoints pause execution so you can examine variables at that moment.

quiz.q: What should you do first when something breaks?
options: Read the error message — it usually names the file and line
quiz.explain: Error messages point at the problem; reading them saves hours.

quiz.q: Why change one thing at a time when debugging?
options: So you know exactly which change fixed the problem
quiz.explain: Changing one variable at a time isolates the cause.

days.title: Polishing Your Portfolio
days.goal: Turn your projects into a portfolio that shows your skill.

video.title: Flexbox vs Grid | Which One Should You Use & Why?

steps: Choose your three best projects and write a one-line description for each.
Add screenshots or live links for every project.
Write a short 'About' section that says what you build and what you are learning.
Check every link and fix any spelling mistakes.
days.task: Publish a portfolio page linking all your course projects with descriptions.
days.challenge: Ask two people to review the portfolio and fix the top complaint from each.

quiz.q: What should a portfolio show?
options: Your best work, with what you built and what it proves
quiz.explain: A portfolio proves skill with real work, not volume.

quiz.q: Why add a short description to each project?
options: It tells visitors what the project does and what you learned
quiz.explain: Context turns a screenshot into evidence of skill.

quiz.q: What is the most common portfolio mistake?
options: Broken links and unfinished projects shown as finished
quiz.explain: Broken links destroy trust instantly.

days.title: Capstone Preparation
days.goal: Plan your final capstone project in detail before building it.

video.title: Learn CSS Flexbox & CSS Grid Building This Dashboard - html and css (CSS Full course 2026)

steps: Write a one-paragraph brief for the site you will build.
List every page and section the site needs.
Sketch the layout for desktop and mobile.
List the data, images and content you need to gather.
days.task: Write a full capstone plan: brief, page list, sketches and a build checklist.
days.challenge: Cut one feature from your plan to keep the build achievable in two days.

quiz.q: Why plan before building the capstone?
options: A plan prevents wasted work and keeps the build focused
It makes the site load faster
quiz.explain: A clear plan means you build once, not three times.

quiz.q: What belongs in a project brief?
options: What you will build, who it is for and what success looks like
quiz.explain: A brief defines the goal, the audience and the definition of done.

quiz.q: Why cut a feature before building?
options: To finish a polished smaller project instead of a broken big one
quiz.explain: Scope discipline is what separates finished projects from abandoned ones.

days.title: Capstone Build and Launch
days.goal: Build your capstone site, test it and deploy it live.

video.title: Become a Fullstack Developer from Scratch

steps: Build the capstone site following your plan, section by section.
Add JavaScript interactivity: at least one form, one dynamic list and one fetch or storage feature.
Test on a phone and a desktop, and fix layout and accessibility issues.
Deploy the finished site and share the live link.
days.task: Ship your capstone: a complete multi-page or single-page site with real interactivity, deployed live.
days.challenge: Record a 60-second walkthrough of your site explaining what you built and why.

quiz.q: What proves a capstone is complete?
options: It works, is deployed and meets the checks in the brief
quiz.explain: A finished, working, deployed project that meets its brief is complete.

quiz.q: What should you test before launch?
options: Links, forms, layout on phone and desktop, and accessibility basics
quiz.explain: Testing the real user paths catches the bugs visitors would hit.

quiz.q: What is the best next step after this course?
options: Keep building small projects and learn a framework like React
quiz.explain: Real projects plus a framework are the natural next step after the fundamentals.

capstone.title: Portfolio Website with Real Interactivity
capstone.brief: Build and deploy a complete portfolio website for yourself or a fictional client. It must have at least three sections, a working contact form with validation, a dynamic project list loaded from JavaScript data, and one feature that fetches or saves data. Deploy it live and share the link.
checks: Site is deployed live and the link works on a phone
At least three sections with clear headings and real content
Contact form validates input and shows success or error messages
Project list is rendered from JavaScript data, not hard-coded HTML
One feature uses fetch or localStorage
Site is responsive with no overflow at 360px
No console errors on any page
deliverables: GitHub repository with the full source code
Screenshots of the site on desktop and mobile
A short written summary of what you built and what you learned
A 60-second video or screen recording walkthrough
